content:
Dear Quillstone Payments AI Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. At Thistlebox, I build and operationalise machine-learning workflows that support business decisions, and I am keen to bring that experience to Quillstone’s work on helping merchants get support quickly and with less friction.

I developed a scheduled LightGBM forecasting workflow in Vertex AI Workbench, producing six-week-ahead forecasts in BigQuery for operational use in Looker. It improved WAPE from 23% to 14% and contributed to an estimated 9% reduction in food waste. I also built an XGBoost churn propensity model with feature engineering and SHAP analysis, with weekly batch scores in BigQuery integrated into dbt workflows for retention targeting. In a holdout, churn fell by 2.1 percentage points in the treated group.

Alongside modelling, I built a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests, writing the application and its Dockerfile; the data platform team handled deployment. I have also started writing pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code, with coverage now at approximately 60%. My daily work with Python, SQL and BigQuery, together with my use of Vertex AI Workbench and dbt, has given me practical experience building data and scoring workflows. My MSc in Statistics provided a foundation in experimental design and modelling uncertainty.

Quillstone’s focus on customer-support automation and its emphasis on ownership, teamwork and learning from mistakes are appealing to me. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience in forecasting, churn modelling and experimentation while continuing to develop as a machine-learning engineer.

Thank you for considering my application.

Kind regards,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, well structured and clearly tailored to the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. It uses specific technologies and quantified outcomes, including the WAPE improvement, estimated food-waste reduction, churn result, and Streamlit adoption. It also accurately distinguishes the candidate’s own work from platform-team deployment responsibility, which supports credibility. The main limitation is not writing quality but role fit: the letter presents strong applied data-science and batch-workflow experience, while the advertised role is focused on production ML engineering, support AI, model serving and MLOps.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The plain-text structure is ATS-friendly: standard paragraphs, no tables, graphics, columns or unusual headings. Relevant terms such as Python, SQL, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt, feature engineering, SHAP, Docker, pytest, Streamlit and scheduled workflows are included naturally. AI screening probability is moderate rather than high because the letter does not contain evidence for several high-priority terms in the advertisement, including chat assistants, RAG, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, MLflow, Kubeflow and Airflow. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than omissions that should be filled with unsupported claims.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the cloud, Python, feature-engineering, batch-scoring, experimentation and quantitative-modelling aspects of the role. It also references ownership, teamwork and learning from mistakes in a credible way based on the company information. However, the candidate material does not show experience with chat assistants or RAG, four years as a machine learning engineer shipping systems to production, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, or the requested MLOps/orchestration tools. The candidate has a Statistics degree rather than a clearly specified machine-learning, computer-science or engineering degree. The document should not imply that scheduled notebooks or SQL batch scoring are equivalent to API model serving or full production MLOps.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the second body paragraph, make the churn validation evidence more precise by changing "In a holdout, churn fell by 2.1 percentage points in the treated group" to "Using a 10% holdout validation, churn fell by 2.1 percentage points in the treated group." This uses the candidate’s documented evidence and makes the result more credible and specific.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the third paragraph, make the nature of the operational experience more ATS-readable without overstating it. Change "My daily work with Python, SQL and BigQuery, together with my use of Vertex AI Workbench and dbt, has given me practical experience building data and scoring workflows" to "My daily work with Python, SQL and BigQuery, together with scheduled notebook jobs in Vertex AI Workbench and weekly batch-scoring workflows integrated with dbt, has given me practical experience operationalising data and scoring workflows."

requirements.requirement: Degree in machine learning, computer science or a related engineering field
At least four years of experience as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production
Experience with AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
Software engineering skills for production systems: model serving, monitoring, data versioning
Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, GCP or Azure)

requirements.quote: "My daily work with Python, SQL and BigQuery"

requirements.requirement: Familiarity with MLOps and orchestration tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or an LLM-observability tool
Experience with feature engineering and data ingestion pipelines
